newsitem.title: JAPAN: TSE mulls forming market for large-lot trading.
newsitem.headline: TSE mulls forming market for large-lot trading.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Tuesday that it was considering creating a market for large-lot cross trading.

The new market, which will also handle basket trading, will offer later trading hours than the TSE cash stock market, which closes at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT), TSE president Mitsuhide Yamaguchi told a news conference.
He also said that the TSE needs stricter penalties for rule violations by member brokerage firms, following a recent scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Basket trading allows orders for various issues to be placed in a single package, while cross trading allows buy and sell orders to be placed simultaneously.
Separately, a TSE spokesman told Reuters that the bourse was not yet considering introducing futures and options on sector indices.
"In general, we do recognise that there are requests for sector-based futures and options, but we cannot say at this point that we are mulling the listing of such instruments," the spokesman said.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Osaka Securities Exchange (OSE) said on Tuesday it was considering listing futures and options on sector indices.
The OSE said it was planning to list futures and options for indices covering the high-technology, consumer and financial sectors.
The OSE also said it was preparing to create a new market by the end of this year for large-lot cross trading and basket trading.
The OSE's new market will trade from 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT) to 5.45 p.m. (0845 GMT), the official said, adding that all issues listed on the OSE would be traded in the new market.

The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said in its evening edition on Tuesday that the creation of the new market was being considered in response to demands from institutional investors ahead of Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms.
